## Q4 (persisted-content detection)
Expected before / observed (frozen test `test_readj_gaps.py::test_G5a_persisted_member_content`, unmodified, c682dd3a; M06 applied to a pristine `git archive` copy, tree `c071b730...`, differing from the pristine copy by exactly one line):
* Unmutated (R08, 3.11.18): 1 passed; all 7 checks CHECK_PASS; persisted `scope.authority_domain` = `customer-refunds`. As expected.
* Mutated M06 (R07, 3.11.18): 1 failed; failed checks exactly `scope_equals_independent_expectation` (persisted `authority_domain` `constant-domain`, the four other scope keys equal the expectation), `scope_authority_domain_equals_manifest_domain` (persisted `constant-domain`), `f4_scope_authority_domain`; the four digest checks pass. As expected. Preflight shows `acp` imported from the M06 copy. Note: the `f4_scope_authority_domain` check row does not log the persisted value (the frozen harness records no detail for it); the value `constant-domain` for that case is inferred from the same expression, not directly recorded. R09 (extra, 3.12.3): identical result.
What is established: with M06 applied, an independent persisted-content assertion (expected value derived from the fixture manifest, not from `scope_identity`) detects the wrong persisted `authority_domain`; unmutated 739efe7 passes it. This is a statement about the harness (mutation adequacy of the persisted-content oracle), reproduced from a pristine copy by this worker.
NOT established: that the binding comparison is sensitive to `authority_domain` (see Q4b); independence of the kill (the G5a test was written by the readjudication session after M06 survival was known, which this worker did not rewrite and is not independent of); anything about production exploitability (other guards refuse a natural domain drift); the original M06 SURVIVED record stands unchanged.

## Q4b (comparison sensitivity, COMPONENT / CLASSIFIER level; D-1 owns the end-to-end graft; no guard disabled or bypassed)
Observed on the pristine copy, 3.11 and 3.12 (R10, R11; all pass):
* B1[pin], B1[f4]: public `configuration_binding_status`: control `bound`; persisted member differing from the live member in exactly `scope.authority_domain` (checked leaf-by-leaf, digest resealed independently) => `mismatch`.
* B2: `ecb.classify` with members equal except `scope.authority_domain` => `mismatch` in both directions; equal members => `bound`.
* B3: `scope_identity` yields different members for two domains and classify => `mismatch`.
Observed on the M06 copy (R13; all pass with variant-keyed expectations): B1 and B2 still `mismatch` for a PERSISTED-side edit to a non-constant value (the value-wise member equality is intact); B3: `scope_identity` returns the identical constant scope for two different domains and classify returns `bound`. Conclusion: the comparison itself (`classify` equality over members) is sensitive to `scope.authority_domain` as a value; M06 removes sensitivity to a domain change at the DERIVATION (`scope_identity`, which feeds both the minted and the live member), so a live-world domain change is invisible to the comparison under M06. This supports the Q4 limit statement.
NOT established: end-to-end live-side refusal for a genuine different domain (D-1); natural reachability (the manifest digest and `authority_domain_mismatch` guards fire first); that a real workflow rebuild with a different live domain is refused by the binding member alone. The probes call `ecb.classify` / `ecb.mint` / `ecb.scope_identity` and the public `configuration_binding_status` directly; they are component-level labels, not claims about `execute`.

* P0 control: claim issued, provision spy called exactly once with the returned claim object, `verify_local_execution_claim` True, no EffectTimeRefusal, no attempt, destination unchanged, one `resolution_checks` row stage `claim`; equal to the materialize control.
* P1 `f4_scalars.status_max_age_seconds`, P2 `scope.authority_domain` (persisted-side), P3 `families.0.effective_policy_digest`, P4 `host_profile_digest`, P5 `effective_profile_digest`; P6 stripped member at cutoff 0; P7/P8 invalid member; P9 unknown version: all `PermissionError("authorization-critical inputs changed before claim issuance")`, spy NOT called, no claim, no new EffectTimeRefusal, no new attempt, unexpected=[] (decisions/attempts/observations/reconciliations unchanged), destination 0 calls and unchanged, exactly one `resolution_checks` row (stage `claim`); equal to the materialize row in type, message, store effects and destination effects. Candidate classifications matched the predictions (mismatch / unbound-after-cutoff / invalid / version-unsupported), recorded as evidence only.
* L1 (single decision stripped, cutoff 1, index 0) and L2 (store generated by the unchanged prior binary b7eb11a, cutoff 1, index 0): claim issued, spy once with the claim, verify True, classification `legacy`, equal to materialize. This documents the known legacy limit.

Observation (recorded per AMEND-R3 semantics, not a failure): every call, accepted or refused, appends 13 `check_events` rows besides one `resolution_checks` row in this fixture; refusals do not write a durable EffectTimeRefusal.
Mutant D06-M04 (R12, copy tree `6b00e015...`, differing in the two mutant lines): control passes; provision rows P1..P5 FAIL (claim issued, spy called once; the materialize reference rows fail too because the body is shared) => M04 KILLED by the provision rows. PREDICTION MISS (recorded, not revised): the frozen per-row split predicted P7, P8, P9 would still pass; they also FAIL under M04 (invalid and unknown-version members are also let through at claim issuance by the mutant). Kill rule satisfied. Also, `-k Q5` matched the module name `test_d2_q4q5`, so all 18 tests ran under M04; Q4b and the other Q5 rows passed there (the Q4b B3 expectation on M04 is the pristine one and it held).
